messages:
Elliot Price: Hey folks — pulling together the docs structure for the KMS hardening/rotation work (tracked in ENG-4246 + docs PR 1187). Need quick alignment on:
1) what’s public vs restricted
2) terminology (KEK/DEK/CMK etc)
3) whether we include screenshots/log examples (and what’s safe)

Proposed structure:
- Public docs site:
  - “Encryption at rest & KMS overview” (high level)
  - “Key rotation: what customers can expect” (cadence + scheduled vs emergency)
  - “Troubleshooting KMS issues (customer-facing)” (symptoms + what to check)
- Restricted (Confluence / ops):
  - SRE runbook: KMS degradation/outage
  - Breakglass policy + approval flow
  - Full failure-mode matrix + game day results

Can Security sanity-check what we’re comfortable publishing?

Kira Thompson: +1. Also question: do we want a separate “Private deployment: customer-managed KMS prerequisites” page? That’s the one customers will actually follow during install/upgrade.

Marcus Lin: Thanks. Generally aligned w/ split.
Public OK:
- Conceptual envelope encryption overview (DEK wrapped by KEK)
- Supported providers and “shared responsibility” boundaries
- Rotation semantics at a product level (scheduled vs emergency, what downtime looks like)

Not public (or at least gated / enterprise-only):
- Concrete failure injection tactics / chaos knobs
- Exact alert thresholds / circuit breaker trip points
- Anything that looks like a playbook for attackers (e.g., “disable key to force fallback X”)

Re screenshots/logs: we should be careful not to leak real key ARNs, account IDs, tenant IDs, region naming, internal endpoint URLs.

Kevin Osei: +1 to Marcus. Also avoid publishing raw audit event schemas verbatim if they include internal field names that map directly to internal services. We can publish “what we log” categories + examples, but keep the canonical schema in restricted docs.

Hanae Suzuki: On Private specifically: customers keep asking “what exact key policy do I need.” We should publish a minimal template / checklist, but avoid giving something too copy-pastable that opens broad permissions.
Maybe: “required actions” list + example that’s intentionally incomplete unless they read the provider docs.

Naomi Feldman: From product POV, we should keep the public docs crisp and not scary.
I like:
- “How rotation works” and “What happens if KMS is unavailable” at a behavior level.
Avoid: “KMS outage runbook” tone.

Simran Kaur: For terminology: please let’s standardize on what we say in sales/security reviews.
Suggestion:
- Use “KEK (Key Encryption Key)” and “DEK (Data Encryption Key)” once, then mostly say “wrapping key” / “data key” in customer-facing docs.
- Use “customer-managed key (CMK)” only when referencing the cloud provider term, and call out it differs by provider.
Also: consistently say “Redwood Hosted / Dedicated / Private” (we’ve mixed “self-hosted” in drafts).

Elliot Price: Super helpful. Re terminology, here’s what’s currently in the draft:
- “KMS key” (generic)
- “CMK” (AWS language)
- “master key” (oops)

I’m going to remove “master key” entirely and stick to KEK/DEK + “KMS key / key in your KMS.”

Kira Thompson: +1 please kill “master key.”
Also for troubleshooting: can we include a table mapping common KMS errors to customer actions? e.g.
- AccessDenied -> check IAM
- NotFound/Disabled -> check key enabled / correct region
- Throttling -> talk to cloud provider / retry

Marcus Lin: Error mapping is fine if generic.
But don’t include our internal retry logic details, and don’t say “bump cache TTL” etc publicly.
Say: “ensure network to KMS endpoints,” “verify key policy allows encrypt/decrypt,” “check key is enabled,” etc.

Kevin Osei: For log examples, we can do sanitized snippets like:
```
level=error msg="kms decrypt failed" provider=aws_kms error="AccessDeniedException" key_id="arn:aws:kms:REGION:ACCOUNT:key/REDACTED" request_id="REDACTED"
```
But no real request IDs, no real tenant IDs. Also keep the message stable with what we actually emit (don’t invent fields we don’t have).

Elliot Price: Good call. I was planning screenshots from Console showing the new “KMS health summary” page, but it’s admin-only. Should we avoid screenshots entirely?

Hanae Suzuki: I’d avoid UI screenshots for now. In Private, customers won’t necessarily have the same UI, and screenshots go stale fast.
Maybe use diagrams (boxes/arrows) + “What you’ll see” bullet lists.

Naomi Feldman: Agree. If we do screenshots, it becomes an expectation that customers can see it.

Kira Thompson: What about *operator* docs (restricted) having screenshots? That might help on-call.

Marcus Lin: Restricted is fine. For restricted screenshots: still redact key IDs/account IDs/tenant IDs, but we can show the internal page.

Simran Kaur: +1. For public: diagrams only.
For restricted: screenshots ok, plus “example incident timeline” is useful.

Elliot Price: OK.
Public docs: no screenshots, only diagrams.
Restricted docs: OK to include screenshots w/ redaction.

Terminology consistency:
- “Key rotation” = changing the active KEK for wrapping new DEKs (and dual-read window until complete)
- “Emergency rotation” = immediate switch + bounded fallback
- “Rotation complete” definition differs Hosted vs Private; we need to phrase carefully.

Can Security confirm what we can safely say for “rotation complete” (esp Private)?

Marcus Lin: For public wording:
- Hosted/Dedicated: “Rotation complete when all active encryption operations use the new key version and remaining artifacts have been rewrapped per policy.”
- Private: “Rotation complete when the deployment is configured to use the new key and validation checks pass. Re-encryption/rewrapping of existing artifacts may occur asynchronously depending on configuration.”
Avoid: giving exact time bounds.

Kevin Osei: Also add: “Old key material must remain available during the transition window to avoid decrypt failures.” That’s a common customer footgun.

Kira Thompson: +1. In the Private rotation procedure we should bold that as a prerequisite: don’t disable old key until validation says OK.

Elliot Price: Great.
Public vs restricted list (draft decision):
PUBLIC
- Overview + provider matrix
- Shared responsibility + customer-managed KMS concept
- Rotation semantics (scheduled/emergency) at high level
- Troubleshooting: generic symptoms + customer checks
- Audit logging: “events we record” categories (no full schema)

RESTRICTED
- Full runbooks (degradation/outage)
- Breakglass access policy details
- Concrete alert thresholds, breaker settings, cache TTL tuning
- Failure-mode matrix + game day results
- Full audit schema + internal event names

Anyone object?

Marcus Lin: Looks good.

Kevin Osei: +1 :thumbsup:

Hanae Suzuki: +1. Only nuance: provider-specific least-priv templates… I think publish minimal required permissions and keep full Terraform/policy snippets in restricted or repo.

Simran Kaur: Agree. For customer-facing, we can say “minimum permissions required: Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/DescribeKey” (and the equivalents) + link to provider docs.

Naomi Feldman: Fine by me.

Kira Thompson: Action items?

Elliot Price: Action items:
- Elliot: update public drafts to remove screenshots + remove “master key” language; add sanitized log snippet guidance.
- Kira: draft troubleshooting table (customer-facing) + flag anything that looks too runbook-ish.
- Marcus/Kevin: review the “audit logging” section to ensure we don’t leak internal schema.
- Hanae: add Private prerequisites checklist text (IAM/key policy pitfalls) but keep full templates restricted.

I’ll ping when the next revision is up in docs PR 1187.

Marcus Lin: Sounds good. Please also add a short “What we mean by customer-managed KMS” callout (some folks think we host their key).

Elliot Price: Will do.
